test_title: SSC Selection Post Matric Level Official Paper (Held On: 30 June, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What was the capital of the Bahmani kingdom at the time of its foundation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gulbarga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Bahmani kingdom, **established in** 1347 **with its capital initially at **Ahsanabad (Gulbarga)** before being moved to** Muhammadabad (Bidar) in 1425,** stood as an independent state from 1347 to 1527.
 
• Organized into four administrative provinces, known as "Taraf," the kingdom comprised *Daultabad, Bidar, Berar, and Gulbarga, *each overseen by a tarafdar or subedar.
 
• The governance of the Bahmani kingdom followed a feudal system.
 
• Encompassing the entirety of the Deccan up to the Krishna river, the Bahmani sultanate reached its zenith of influence during the tenure of Mahmud Gawan as vizier from 1466 to 1481.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gulbarga**, situated in the Indian state of Karnataka, serves as the administrative center of the Kalaburagi district and stands as the largest city in North Karnataka (Kalyana-Karnataka). 
 
• Positioned 568 km north of Bangalore, the state capital, Kalaburagi was integrated into the newly formed Mysore State (now Karnataka) under the States Reorganisation Act in 1956. 
 
• Noteworthy architectural wonders from the Bahamani Kingdom era adorn Kalaburagi, including the Jama Masjid within Kalaburagi Fort. Moreover, Kalaburagi hosts the circuit bench of the High Court of Karnataka. 
 
• In 2014, UNESCO placed several structures in the city on its "tentative list" for potential recognition as a World Heritage Site, along with others in the vicinity, under the collective name Monuments and Forts of the Deccan Sultanate.
